questions.question: Which festival is known as the 'festival of lights'?
questions.funFact: On Diwali, people light rows of lamps to celebrate the victory of good over evil.

questions.question: Which festival is known as the 'festival of colours'?
questions.funFact: On Holi, people throw coloured powders and splash water to welcome the spring season.

questions.question: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated at the end of the holy month of ___.
questions.funFact: During Ramadan, many Muslims fast from dawn to sunset, and Eid is the happy feast at the end.

questions.question: Onam is a harvest festival celebrated mainly in Kerala.
questions.funFact: During Onam, people in Kerala make beautiful flower designs called 'pookalam' and hold snake-boat races.

questions.question: On Raksha Bandhan, a sister ties a special thread called a ___ on her brother's wrist.
questions.funFact: The rakhi stands for a brother's promise to always protect and care for his sister.

questions.question: Match each festival to the state it is most linked with.
questions.funFact: India is so diverse that a festival being celebrated in one state may be little known in another.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT mainly a harvest festival?
questions.funFact: Pongal, Baisakhi and Onam all celebrate the harvest, while Diwali celebrates light and goodness.

questions.question: Ganesh Chaturthi, celebrating Lord Ganesha, is celebrated most grandly in which state?
questions.funFact: In Maharashtra, huge clay statues of Ganesha are worshipped for days and then placed in water.

questions.question: Christmas is celebrated on 25 December.
questions.funFact: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ and is enjoyed by people all around the world.

questions.question: During Diwali, people light small oil lamps called ___.
questions.funFact: Diyas are little clay lamps filled with oil and a cotton wick that glow warmly at night.

questions.question: Durga Puja is celebrated with the most grandeur in which state?
questions.funFact: During Durga Puja in West Bengal, artists build giant decorated tents called 'pandals' for the goddess.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated by flying kites, especially in Gujarat in January?
questions.funFact: On Makar Sankranti, the skies over Gujarat fill with thousands of colourful kites.
